column1: # Per-cell Excel `num_fmt` override: when an .xlsx cell carries a date
# format string that doesn't round-trip through the canonical 1-2-3
# should display the value the way Excel would — and re-save the
# original `num_fmt` string verbatim if the cell hasn't been touched.
# Layout on sheet A (all cells = serial 36540 = Saturday, 2000-01-15):
# Widen column A so the long forms (10..12 chars) fit without overflow
# A1 displays the Excel format string verbatim, not the canonical D-letter
# rendering ("00-JAN-15" or similar would mean the override missed).
# A2: title-case month abbreviation, 4-digit year, no leading zero on day.
# A3: weekday name spelled out — only reachable through the override path.
# A4: canonical 1-2-3 D1 form. The xlsx string `dd-mmm-yy` matches
# `to_num_fmt(DateDmy)` exactly so no override is stored — the cell
# renders through the canonical D1 path (uppercase month abbrev).
# Save → reload round-trip: write the workbook back to a temp xlsx,
# then `/File Retrieve` it and verify the same renderings still appear.
# A round-trip-safe override is the only way A3 survives — saving the
# canonical `m/d` and reloading would render "1/15" not "Saturday".
# Reload the just-saved file and re-check.
# Need to widen column A again on the freshly-loaded workbook since
# /File Retrieve resets column widths to whatever the xlsx carried
# (the original fixture didn't set a custom width).
